questions.markdown:
Let $S=\{a,b,c\}$ and $P(S)$ be the power set of $S$. Then draw the Hasse diagram of the poset $(P(S),\subseteq)$. Is it a lattice? Justify your answer.

Also list all the antichains of length more than one in the poset $P(S)$.

i. Verify whether the following lattice is distributive. Justify your answer.

ii. If a lattice $(A,\leq)$ is distributive then show that for any elements $a,b,c$ in $A$, $(a\vee b)\wedge c \leq a\vee (b\wedge c)$

questions.markdown: Let $E(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\overline{x_1}\vee\overline{\bigl(\overline{x_2}\vee\overline{(\overline{x_3}\wedge x_1)}\bigr)}$ be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra $\{0,1\},\vee,\wedge,\overline{\phantom{x}}$. Write $E(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ in both disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms.
Determine the number of integers between 1 and 250 (including 1 and 250) that are not divisible by any of the integers 2,3,5 and 7.
Show that the number of partitions of $n$ is equal to the number of partitions of $2n$ which have exactly $n$ parts.
Find the 60th permutation of the five marks $0,1,2,3,4$ in Fike's order.

questions.markdown:
i) Prove that a nonempty subset $H$ of a group $(G,*)$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $a*b^{-1}\in H$ for every $a,b\in H$.

ii) Define $*$ on $\mathbb{R}-\{0\}$ as $a*b=\dfrac{ab}{5}$, for all $a,b\in \mathbb{R}-\{0\}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ is a set of all real numbers. Show that $(\mathbb{R}-\{0\},*)$ forms an abelian group.
If $G$ is any graph with 6 vertices then show that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ contains a triangle.

Solve

$$
\begin{aligned}
2x_1+x_2-x_3&=1\\
x_1+2x_2+x_3&=8\\
-x_1+x_2-x_3&=-5
\end{aligned}
$$

by LU decomposition method.

i. If $G$ is a finite group and $H$ a subgroup of $G$, then show that the order of $H$ divides the order $G$.

ii. Is the group $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ under the operation “multiplication modulo 7” cyclic? Justify your answer.
In a tree with 14 pendant vertices, the degree of every non-pendant vertex is either 4 or 5. Find the number of vertices of degree 4 and 5, respectively.
Using Dijkstra's algorithm, find the shortest paths from 's' to all the other vertices.

Find a singular value decomposition of the matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
2&0\\
0&1\\
1&0
\end{bmatrix}
$$
Show that $s\vee r$ is tautologically implied by the premises $p\vee q$, $p\to r$, and $q\to s$.
Prove that $(\exists x)(D(x)\wedge A(x)),\ (\forall x)(A(x)\to C(x))\Rightarrow (\exists x)(D(x)\wedge C(x)).$
